chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Writing the Apollo shows and the hardest music he could
summary: He wrote all the show music under time pressure, passed some off to an assistant, and says he always wrote difficult scores to learn.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You had to get all the kids together and get their music.

I had to write all the music for the show and then I'd give it to -- I turned that over to a girl because it got too tough for me, I couldn't -- you know, Monday the show would meet in rehearsal and probably the ingenue wasn't in and I had to wait till she comes in to get her key that she sings a song in so I could arrange it for her. And that would be on a Tuesday and now I got to write three numbers, see, and oh, I used to sometimes Don Redmond used to say, you write all this, and I'd say yeah. You're good.
Don Redmon was a band leader. He used to play with the McKinney Cottonpickers, didn't he. He was left-handed. He was a left-handed conductor too.

Yeah, he was a great guy. And a lot of them other guys used to come to me and tell me, don't write so hard music. I said I ain't writing -- because I always used to try to write the hardest music I could, because I wanted to learn. When Duke Ellington used to come in, and say, don't write only two saxes and three saxes and two trumpets and a trombone, that's all. I said the man tells me to write a whole orchestration.
